# Frequently asked questions

Short answers to the questions that come up most often with this project. For
deeper coverage, follow the linked guides.

---

## General

**Q: What exactly is this project?**

A: An STM32CubeIDE firmware for the NUCLEO-H743ZI2 that runs Azure RTOS
ThreadX + NetX Duo, listens for UDP text commands on port 6000 over IPv4 and
IPv6, controls the green LED, and reports the user button state over UDP.

**Q: Why is IPv6 not generated by CubeMX?**

A: The CubeMX Azure RTOS integration does not emit the IPv6 enable and address
calls. They are hand-added in the `USER CODE` block of `app_netxduo.c`, with
the matching library options in `nx_user.h`. See
[IPV6_AND_NETWORKING.md](IPV6_AND_NETWORKING.md).

**Q: Can I regenerate the project from the `.ioc`?**

A: Yes, but keep the `USER CODE` blocks; the IPv6 setup and the whole
application thread live in them. See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md).

**Q: Do I need STM32CubeIDE?**

A: The checked-in `Debug/` makefile allows command-line builds, but the
reference workflow is STM32CubeIDE. See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md).

---

## Networking

**Q: Why is the IP address static?**

A: The ST example hard-codes `192.168.1.111` so the demo works without a DHCP
server. Change it to a free address in your subnet; DHCP can be added, see
[EXTENDING.md](EXTENDING.md).

**Q: The IPv6 address is for another network. What do I do?**

A: Edit the four words at `app_netxduo.c` lines 265 to 268 to match your
router's /64 prefix. The recipe is in
[TROUBLESHOOTING.md](TROUBLESHOOTING.md).

**Q: Why does the board not respond on IPv6?**

A: Most likely the hard-coded /64 does not match your network, or your router
does not route IPv6. Try link-local testing, see
[IPV6_AND_NETWORKING.md](IPV6_AND_NETWORKING.md).

**Q: Which port should the PC listen on for button reports?**

A: UDP 55100 (the default). The board sends `BUTTON:0` / `BUTTON:1` there.

**Q: Can I use TCP?**

A: TCP is enabled in the stack but no TCP socket is created. Add one as shown
in [EXTENDING.md](EXTENDING.md).

**Q: How fast can the board send UDP?**

A: The button reporter is throttled to one datagram every ~200 ms. The
Ethernet link is 100 Mbit/s and NetX Duo can go much faster; the limit here is
deliberate (see `SEND_SLEEP_TICKS`).

**Q: What happens if the packet pool runs out?**

A: `nx_packet_allocate` fails with `NX_NO_PACKET` and `send_udp_message`
drops the packet. Watch `NxAppPool.nx_packet_pool_available` in the debugger;
increase `NX_APP_PACKET_POOL_SIZE` if needed.

---

## Hardware and firmware

**Q: Which board does this target?**

A: NUCLEO-H743ZI2 (STM32H743ZIT6, LQFP144). See
[GPIO_AND_BOARD.md](GPIO_AND_BOARD.md).

**Q: Why is the Ethernet RAM placed at 0x30040000?**

A: That is RAM_D2 (SRAM3), outside the cached RAM_D1, so DMA descriptors stay
coherent. See [MEMORY_LAYOUT.md](MEMORY_LAYOUT.md).

**Q: Why do I see no console output?**

A: Check the COM port, 115200 8N1 settings, and whether the firmware flashed;
the firmware hangs in `Error_Handler()` silently if init fails. See
[TROUBLESHOOTING.md](TROUBLESHOOTING.md).

**Q: The LED does not turn on when I send `LED ON`.**

A: Check that the payload reaches port 6000 (console echoes it), then check
the parser: `LED ON`, `LED_ON`, `LEDON`, or `ON` all work; `LEDONX` contains
`LED` and `ON` substrings too. See [PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md).

**Q: Is the MAC address configurable?**

A: Yes, in `Core/Src/main.c`, lines 229 to 234 (`MACAddr[]`). Avoid the ST
reserved OUI only if you plan commercial use.

---

## Development

**Q: How do I debug the firmware?**

A: STM32CubeIDE debug session, breakpoints in `nx_app_thread_entry`,
`Error_Handler`, etc. See [DEBUGGING.md](DEBUGGING.md).

**Q: How much memory is free?**

A: About 30 KB for the NetX byte pool, ~21 KB used by defaults, leaving a few
KB headroom; RAM_D1 holds the normal program data. See
[MEMORY_LAYOUT.md](MEMORY_LAYOUT.md).

**Q: Where do I report a bug?**

A: Open an issue using the templates, or a PR following
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

**Q: Why no em dashes in the docs?**

A: Repository style choice: hyphens, commas, and parentheses are used instead
throughout the documentation.
